title: Indonesia Parcel Logistics
thesis: Snowflake turns daily hub data from a synthetic Indonesian parcel network into on-time delivery KPIs, 7-day disruption-risk scores, dwell-time anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: On-time delivery, disruptions, failed attempts and parcels handled for 30 hubs across 6 cities.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to hub-day rows.
The late-parcels chart shows which disruption causes make the most parcels late.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of delivery KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which hubs are likely to cause the next disruption?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each hub's probability of a disruption in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags parcel dwell-time outliers per hub, and the forecast projects network-wide parcel volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the hubs behind those risks?

talking_points: Sorter uptime and fleet readiness frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against on-time delivery by hub shows where discipline and service move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, disruption, cause and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a hub sorter alarms right now?

talking_points: Live hub sorter readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the hub's current risk band, then emails the planner.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
